events.text: {npc} has been thrown to the very edge of the jade platform, one hand on the rim and the open sky beneath. The immortals watching from the next isle have stopped talking. It is yours to say what happens now.

choices.text: Pull {him} back from the edge, and walk away

effects.log: You pull {him} back onto the jade and turn your back. That is the whole answer.

choices.text: Leave {him} a wound the clouds will not wash out

effects.log: You make sure {he} will feel this bout for a long century.

choices.text: Break the core {he} cultivated for a thousand years

effects.log: You lay two fingers on the place where an immortal keeps everything.

choices.text: End it. This was to the death

effects.log: You do not look away.

choices.text: Hear the oath {he} offers

effects.log: {He} swears it on the jade with the open sky beneath.

events.text: The wind has carried {npc}'s sword off the isle, and {npc} lets it go. {He} sits back on the cloud-grass and waits, an immortal who has lived long enough to know how these things end.

choices.text: "Go find your sword"

effects.log: {He} looks at you as if you had spoken a strange tongue, and then goes.

choices.text: Take something {he} will have to grow back

effects.log: It is not quick. {He} does not cry out, which you note.

choices.text: Close the core, so {he} never climbs again

effects.log: {He} understands what you mean to do a moment before you do it.

choices.text: Finish what the bout began

effects.log: You do not look away.

choices.text: Take {his} oath instead

effects.log: {He} swears it on the jade with the open sky beneath.

events.text: Lightning is still crawling over the stones where {npc} fell. {He} comes up on one elbow and spits out the taste of it. "An old rule of the Isles," {he} says. "The winner chooses. Choose, then."

choices.text: "Then I choose to be done"

effects.log: You sheathe your blade. {npc} laughs once, short, and lies back down.

choices.text: Choose a lesson

effects.log: You give {him} a lesson for the next few hundred years.

choices.text: Choose the hardest one

effects.log: You choose, and the lightning on the stones goes out.

choices.text: Make sure {he} never climbs back up

effects.log: You do not look away.

choices.text: Let {him} swear it on the jade

effects.log: {He} swears it on the jade with the open sky beneath.

events.text: A drifting isle you have never seen before comes alongside yours at dawn, and {npc} is standing on its edge. {He} has climbed since you last met; the clouds bend around {him} now. "I have counted the years," {he} says. "All of them."

choices.text: Step across and settle it

ok.log: This time {npc} is the one on the stones, and {he} does not get up quickly. Something in {his} face has changed.

fail.log: {npc} has learned every one of your openings. {He} steps back onto {his} isle and lets it drift away, laughing.

choices.text: Talk with {him} across the gap

effects.log: You talk until the isles drift apart. At the end of it {he} only looks tired.

choices.text: Let the isles part

effects.log: {He} watches you all the way out of sight.

events.text: There is a new name on the challenge board of the Jade Court, written in a hand you know: {npc}. Under it, in smaller characters, the hour and the platform, and the words "no seconds".

choices.text: Be on the platform at the hour

ok.log: You leave {npc} kneeling on the jade, and the Court has something new to talk about.

fail.log: It goes {his} way from the first exchange. {He} bows to you very correctly, which is worse than laughing.

choices.text: Write under it: "Not today"

effects.log: The Court talks about that too.

choices.text: Go to {his} grotto instead, and ask why

effects.log: You sit outside {his} grotto until {he} comes out. You talk until the stars turn. It ends there.

events.text: {npc} finds you on the cloud road between two isles, where there is nowhere to step aside. {He} is stronger, and {he} wants you to see it. "Every century I thought of you," {he} says. "It helped."

choices.text: Then let it help {him} now

ok.log: It does not help {him} enough. {He} goes down on the cloud road and stays there.

fail.log: It helps {him} plenty. You end up on your back on the cloud road, looking at the sky, and {he} walks over you.

choices.text: Offer {him} the road and nothing else

effects.log: You step to the very edge and let {him} pass. {He} hates that more than a fight.

choices.text: Ask what {he} would do with the win

effects.log: The question stops {him}. In the end {he} has no answer, and goes home to look for one.

events.text: An immortal of {npc}'s house comes to your grotto with two attendants and no greeting. "You hurt one of ours on the platforms," {he} says. "I am the one who answers for our house."

choices.text: Answer {him} on the platform

ok.log: {npc} goes down in front of {his} own attendants. {He} leaves without a word, and you know whose door {he} goes to next.

fail.log: {npc} puts you down on the jade and leaves you there for the attendants to see.

choices.text: Bow, and ask the house's pardon

effects.log: You bow to an immortal who has done nothing to earn it. {npc} lets the bow last.

events.text: {npc} does not come in person. {He} sends a jade slip with your name on it and a single line: the platform at the third bell, for what was done to one of mine.

choices.text: Go to the third bell

ok.log: By the fourth bell it is {npc} who needs the healer. {He} will not forget it, and neither will {his} house.

fail.log: By the fourth bell it is you who needs one. The house is satisfied, for now.

choices.text: Send the slip back with your apology written under it

effects.log: The apology costs you more than a bout would have. The house takes it.

events.text: The old master of {npc}'s house comes up to your isle on foot, which nobody of that age does. The clouds go still around {him}. "My people keep losing to you," {he} says mildly. "So now it is me."

choices.text: Face the master

ok.log: The old master goes down on one knee on your isle, and gets up slowly, and bows. Nobody from that house will ever come up your steps again.

fail.log: {npc} stops your blade with two fingers and hands it back to you. "There," {he} says. "Now we are even."

choices.text: Kneel, and offer nothing but the bow

effects.log: You kneel on your own isle. The old master lets you kneel until the clouds move, and then goes home.

events.text: Every immortal of {npc}'s house has gone quiet this season, and you know why: the master is coming. When {he} arrives it is with no attendants and no hurry, and {he} sits down on your steps to wait for you.

choices.text: Go out to {him}

ok.log: You go out, and it is the longest fight of your life, and at the end of it the old master is the one sitting on the steps. Neither of you says anything for a while.

fail.log: The old master is gentle about it, which is the worst part.

choices.text: Go out and kneel on the step below {him}

effects.log: {He} looks down at you for a long time. Then {he} stands, and goes, and the house is done with you.

events.text: An immortal with an old scar across both palms is waiting for you outside the long hall of your order. "Your teacher in this order shamed me before a whole isle, a thousand years ago," {he} says. "You will do."

choices.text: Then let me do

ok.log: {npc} ends on the jade, looking up. "So the teaching held," {he} says, and it costs {him} something.

fail.log: {npc} stands over you a while. "Tell your teacher I am still here," {he} says.

choices.text: Ask {him} to tell you what happened, all of it

effects.log: It is a very long story and a very old one. By the end {he} is tired of carrying it, and you carry a piece of it for {him}.

choices.text: Walk past {him} into the hall

effects.log: You feel {his} eyes all the way in.

events.text: Someone has left a sword on the doorstep of your grotto, point down in the stone, with a jade slip tied to the hilt: the grudge of a thousand years ago is owed by the student now. {npc} is sitting on the next rock, eating a cloud-pear.

choices.text: Pull the sword out of the stone and hand it back

ok.log: You hand it back, and then you show {him} what the teaching was. {He} takes the sword home with a new respect.

fail.log: {He} takes the sword back and shows you what the teaching was missing.

choices.text: Sit down and ask for half the pear

effects.log: {He} gives you half. You eat in silence. Then {he} tells you everything, and the grudge is lighter by the end.

choices.text: Leave the sword where it is

effects.log: It stays in the stone. So does the grudge.

events.text: Your core has been cracked for years now, and the Isles know it. A cloud-ferryman leans over while you cross and says, low, that there is a recluse on the Ninth Cloud who mended a broken core once, a long time ago.

choices.text: Ask the ferryman the way

effects.log: The ferryman tells you the way, and refuses the fare.

choices.text: Thank the ferryman and say nothing more

effects.log: You thank the ferryman. The name stays with you anyway.

events.text: A slip of jade arrives with no sender. Inside, in a steady hand: "A cracked core can be closed. I have done it once. The Ninth Cloud, the white pagoda, before the next gathering."

choices.text: Go to the white pagoda

effects.log: You set out, slower than you once were.

choices.text: Put the slip away for now

effects.log: You put it in a drawer. You take it out often.

events.text: The recluse of the white pagoda is very small and very old, and does not like you. "It can be closed," the recluse says. "Not by stones. By a year of grinding star-salt in the cold, and a herb from the underside of the isle that nobody young will climb for."

choices.text: Grind the star-salt for a year

effects.log: A year of cold hands and salt. At the end the recluse looks at you differently.

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: You go back down. The recluse does not watch you leave.

events.text: The recluse listens to your core for an hour, the way someone listens to a bell with a crack in it. "A season of needles of cloud-iron," the recluse says at last. "And patience. You have none. You will have to grow some."

choices.text: Stay the season, and grow some

effects.log: A season of needles. Somewhere in it you find a little patience, which surprises you both.

choices.text: Leave, for now

effects.log: You go. The crack goes with you.

events.text: Everything is ready: the salt, the herb, the needles, a cold room at the top of the pagoda. The recluse says it plainly: closing a core hurts more than the cracking did, and some immortals stop it halfway.

choices.text: Do not stop it halfway

effects.log: Three days and three nights in the cold room. You do not stop it.

choices.text: Not today

effects.log: The recluse covers the needles. They will keep.

events.text: The last step, the recluse says, is yours alone: the core is closed from inside, with your own energy, and you will have to go looking for that energy in the dark where it leaked away.

choices.text: Go into the dark after it

effects.log: You find it far down, a thread of warmth in the cold, and you follow it back up.

choices.text: Ask for more time

effects.log: The recluse gives you time as if it were nothing at all.
